utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, with you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is the case IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber received a message at that Mr. Groome could not arrive in time today and that he's expected sometime during the first session and that you, Mr. Weber, and you, Ms. Marcus, would take over temporarily. That's on the record. We're waiting for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stoparic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Jordash will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I want to move swiftly through the events in SBWS and move into Bosnia very quickly. Am I correct that in relation to the attack on Tovarnik, this was a JNA operation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If my memory serves me, it was the Kraljevo Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And it was designed to create a passageway for the JNA?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The goal was to create a passage to Vukovar and lift the blockade from the Vukovar barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And there were 70 of you volunteers under the command of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, am I correct that when you moved into Bosnia, you personally, the operations you conducted were also within the subordination of the army?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning under the command of the JNA and until a certain moment when the JNA withdrew from Bosnia-Herzegovina. Before that moment, we were always under the JNA command.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And is this right: You would -- you would return to Sid, you personally, with a number of volunteers, between operations at various war fronts in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that I always returned home. I always spent some time there for furlough.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: For furlough. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, furlough. I needed to take a break from everything that was going on in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. And the JNA would request volunteers from the municipal SCP, is that correct, in Sid?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you explain what the situation was?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned the SPS. I don't know that the SPS ever organised any volunteers. It was the SRS, the Serbian Radical Party. But it wasn't the Municipal Board of Sid. The JNA did not talk to each Municipal Board separately. They spoke to the Crisis Staff and the Main Board of the Serbian Radical Party in Belgrade, and then at the local level they organised volunteers. The list of volunteers were handed over to the JNA, and the transport of those volunteers was then organised to a place where combat would take place, where we would be engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you for the explanation. Now, in mid-April of 1992, did you go to Trebinje in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the date as I sit here today, but I was in Trebinje in Bosnia, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And is this how it occurred, that in the first part of 1992, you were asked to find SRS, SCP volunteers to go to the battle-field in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned Trebinje a minute ago, and that's in Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let me just take you back a bit. Is it correct that during the first part of 1992, Milenko Petric told you to find SRS/SCP volunteers to go to the battle-field in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On three occasions I was requested to gather the volunteers I knew for engagement in Bosnia, and I suppose that one of those occasions was in the first half of 1992. I can't recall the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And were you asked by Milenko Petric to do that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milenko Petric was the president of the Municipal Board of the Serbian Radical Party, and also for a while he was the president of the district board for Srem, also of the Serbian Radical Party, and, yes, he was the one who conveyed that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did you, following that request, then go with a group of volunteers to Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I went to Belgrade, and then from Belgrade I went to Podgorica, and then from Podgorica to Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that the group of volunteers that you went with then fell under the command of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We joined another unit of volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party which was billeted outside of Trebinje at facility called Grab, and the commander of that unit was Branislav Vakic. And the brigade commander in my view was Colonel Glusalic or something to that effect. He represented the JNA, and the JNA was later on transformed into the Army of Republika Srpska, and he belonged to either/or, but I believe that he served under the JNA at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And let me try to shortcut things. You then went from Trebinje to Nevesinje, is that correct, with your group of volunteers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit that I belonged to and that was billeted in Trebinje sent me and a few other men to assist the unit in Nevesinje. In other words, not all of the unit went to Nevesinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And you went there and, again, you were under whose command?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a parachute unit, and the colonel was there, Colonel Magic. That's how he introduced himself to us. He gave us communication means, and he was the -- in charge of the operation and that Colonel Glusalic or Glusic, I'm not sure about the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Am I correct that you went with the same group of volunteers to Mostar to engage in military operations?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not engaged in Mostar. There was an offensive, and we were actually chased away from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you under the command of a JNA colonel?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, usually the brigade commander is either a colonel or a lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, just factually and actually, were you under the command of the brigade commander whilst in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, every location had its commander, and that commander was usually the commander of the brigade that was responsible for the territory. There were also commanders at lower levels, at the battalion level, at the sector level, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And during -- there are more operations during this period, including, am I correct, in Capljina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around Capljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And is it correct that during these operations or when these operations finished you would travel back to Sid at times for a break from the war, for furlough?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If an operation went on for three or four days -- or, rather, let's -- let me put it in very simple terms. I was never anywhere for longer than two months, but if there were five operations within those two months, I didn't go home between the operations. I just took a short break at a temporary base.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. But after two months you would then head home to Sid?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, approximately two months. After two months, I would ask to be allowed to go home to rest. But that was the system that was in place. The entire volunteer unit would spend a maximum of two months in an area, and then they would be sent home to rest and replaced by other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Replaced by other volunteer groups who were also coming from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. The Yugoslav People's Army decided who, where, and when, how many reservists they needed. You see, a volunteer is one and the same as a reservist. A volunteer was invited, was called to come, whereas reservists volunteered to come, but they had the identical obligations and rights.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And so it was quite normal at that point in time for volunteers to come from Serbia, form groups, and then be subordinated to the army?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fortunately enough, that's the kind of people we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there's a war going on, we all try to take part.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, there came a time when you formed your own group of about 200 people; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the founders, not independently, not on my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Who else was involved in forming that group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Mirko Zugic and a few other men whom I'd not known before that. Major Mirko Zugic from Novi Sad introduced me to those men who wanted to set up a volunteer unit that would not be affiliated with any political party.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And where did you recruit from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly from Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And where did you -- where did you receive your weapons from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received weapons at the Brcko barracks from Colonel Paja Milenkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So was the situation that you travelled -- the men who were recruits travelled in small groups into Bosnia and then attended at Brcko barracks?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there waiting for them in Brcko, and they had travelled at their own expense, to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Individually and in small groups?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And upon arriving at Brcko barracks, you then received, is it correct, all your supplies from the VRS?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. However, before that we received from confirmations or IDs from Djordje Ristanic, who was the mayor of the city, and that was in recognition of our citizenship of Republika Srpska as well as of the state of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you explain that a bit further. What do you mean your citizenship of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's how it was. That was document showing that I was recognised as a citizen of Republika Srpska, as well as my already existing citizenship of the Republic of Yugoslavia. In other words, this was in recognition of my dual citizenship.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And was this offered to you then as a -- if you like, a recognition of your contribution to the war effort in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was a condition for my unit to legally join the Army of Republika Srpska. At least that was one of the conditions that prevailed in the municipality of Brcko, a condition that had to be met.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So volunteers who went to fight in Brcko had to take on citizenship of the Republika Srpska in order to fight?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the case with my unit, the unit that I organised together with Mirko Zugic. Maybe there were units of volunteers which did not have to undergo such procedures. We came on our own, of our own will, and we wanted to be equal members of the Army of Republika Srpska. The mayor of the city of Brcko came up with this solution. He offered it to us, we is accepted it, and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And at this point in time, am I correct that you received no instructions from anyone within Serbia to travel and form a volunteer unit within Bosnia? You did it on your own say so.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A group of my acquaintances and myself, and the answer's yes, we did it have our own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And would you accept this: That it was relatively easy for someone, even -and I mean this with no disrespect - a low-level soldier like yourself to do exactly the same, gather men and form volunteer units within Bosnia -- gather men from Serbia, I mean, and form volunteer units within Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You had to be known. Somebody had to know you. You had to have the image of man who had fought before, who had some experience. But, yes, you're right. Different people, different groups could join any of the units along the front line. However, what we did, that was a bit more serious. Two hundred men, citizenship, under the command of the Army of Republika Srpska. We were no paramilitary unit at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And let me ask you this: Whilst in Brcko, were you involved in cleansing territory?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some villages around Brcko, some parts of the town that hadn't been cleansed before.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, there are some who think that "cleansing" was a term which implied attacking civilians. What do you say it meant?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've answered this question for countless times now. "Cleansing" is a strictly military term, that is cleansing or mopping up, which means you go out in the field and you want to mop it up and clear it of any enemy soldiers. Now, whether you capture individuals, take individuals prisoner, or kill anyone in the process, whatever you do, at the end of that process, you will say that you will have mopped up the area and cleared it of any enemy soldiers. Civilians have nothing to do with that process.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you were interviewed by the Prosecution, not necessarily this Prosecution -- let's forget this Prosecution for a moment, but when you were interviewed previously to testify, were you being pushed to define "cleansing" in a different way? Is that why you were kept being asked about cleansing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nearly everyone asked, and nobody asked me to define it in any different way or that I should change my definition. They merely wanted to know what "cleansing" or "mopping up" was, and I always provided the same definition. I know there is a term "ethnic cleansing." Now, the term we use in the army, which is that of mopping up, in that sense it has nothing to do with that other term.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, whilst you were in Brcko, you came across a man called Zika Crnogorac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that you joined the group he had to assist with taking over Brcko?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No. We had a joint mop-up operation, but not in the town of Brcko. The place was called Fazanerija or something like that. And I didn't join his group. We each had our own groups, and we jointly mopped up the area called Fazanerija. That's something that I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that from what you observed, Crnogorac acted in a professional manner whilst commanding his group?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were special units, and they were an elite unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did you observe him acting in any improper manner toward civilians?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was billeted in the barracks, and they were billeted elsewhere. There were some stories surrounding Zika Crnogorac involving problems with the civilian authorities, but I, myself, didn't observe anything, and I can only speculate. That wouldn't be relevant, would it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let me take you to your statement so we can shortcut this.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, 1D1720.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Whilst that is happening, did Zika Crnogorac arrive in Bosnia and form his own unit, as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he had a unit. I don't know how it came into existence, who put it together. Perhaps he wasn't its commander at all. I just remember the name, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, don't you know, Mr. Witness, that he came to the area of Brcko and selected men to join his unit?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. When he left, there was a special unit called Pesa. He may have trained them. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, did Crnogorac's men that you saw him with have any equipment that others didn't have?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their gather was better, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Which gear was better?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these fellows'.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Which gear that these fellows had was better, and how was it better?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It resembled NATO gear. I don't remember anymore, but at any rate, it was much more practical and better than the one I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Are you talking about the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, uniforms. Oh, well, as far as weapons are concerned -- perhaps you thought of weapons. I don't remember that. I think they had weapons of our local make. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. So --

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to bear in mind that it was 1992, and I forgot a great deal.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, there is -- there's nothing, then, that sticks in your mind now concerning any difference between the weapons that Crnogorac's men had and those that other groups, such as your own, had? Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Visually they appeared different, and I don't remember about the weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's actually go to your -- another statement, the first statement, P1702. While that's coming up, are you suggesting that Crnogorac had a separate unit to the Pesa unit, or are you saying they're one and the same?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure myself, but I don't think that they existed at the same time. Perhaps Pesa's unit grew out of the other one. I'm not sure. At a time when Pesa's unit was popular, the man Crnogorac was no longer mentioned. He had probably gone by then. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So, let's just deal then with Crnogorac before Pesa's unit. Am I correct that you do not know where Crnogorac or his men were trained, the location?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not sure that I do know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you know where Pesa's men were trained?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were always training in their own camp. As for their earlier training, well, I knew Pesa personally -- or the late, Pesa, I should say. He was killed. And on several occasions I carried out some operations with them jointly, and they were very good fighters. They did have training at some location in a camp. They told me, but I've forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And am I correct that you do not know whether Crnogorac's men, prior to Pesa, were from Serbia or from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot state with absolute certainty either way. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 61 of this statement, which is page 12 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek clarification on one issue. You said that you knew Pesa personally. Where did you get to know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Brcko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You didn't know him from before you went to Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He was born in the area around Brcko. I also know his deputy, Pantic, as well as -- well, I knew the names of some of his best commanders as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just take instructions, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And Pesa's men were from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. One of them was from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And who did Crnogorac take orders from whilst he was in the area?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that there was this one action where his men and my men jointly worked in the mopping-up of Fazanerija. Now, I suppose the order came from Commander Milenkovic. I'm not sure. I don't know. At a later date, there was Kutlasic, so it must have come from some of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's go back, then, to Milenkovic. Did you receive your orders from him concerning this mopping-up exercise?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would often go to Paja Milenkovic's office for meetings whenever we would be summoned, because we had a phone in our quarters, and he'd ring us up and tell us that we should come see him. And he would tell us then what the plan was for a job that needed doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And were you summonsed along with Crnogorac prior to the operation in Fazanerija?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We met up in a meadow next to a forest. We looked at maps on the hood of a car, made a plan, formed a skirmish line and headed into the mop-up operation. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: All right. And Pesa's unit was a special unit of the VRS, is that correct, subordinated to the VRS?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Kutlasic would spend more time with Pesa's men in the school building where their base was than in his own office in the barracks. Yes. It was a legendary special unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And was Zika Crnogorac very close to Pesa when they were -- were they close together as people, I mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Did it -- did there come a point when Crnogorac tried to subordinate the VRS to him rather than the reverse?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's something that I referred to initially when you asked me about Brcko, when I said that there were problems with local authorities. Some individuals were expelled from the territory of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And at that included Crnogorac?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not absolutely sure, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me take you, before I move on this subject, to one paragraph. I apologise to Madam Registrar for jumping from statement to statement, but can we go, please, to 1D1720. And to page -- before we go, we move, can you have a look at that and just confirm that your signature is on that document, and it relates to statements taken -- or interviews you had with the Prosecution between the 20th of February, 2004, and 15th of November, 2005? I apologise again. I'm going to leave this for my co-accused to deal with. Let's move on to the Skorpions, and I'll just leave that topic there for now. Now, am I correct that when you joined the Skorpions, you regarded that new post as a promotion in part because the Skorpions were considered to be a disciplined unit, unlike some that you'd been part of prior to that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the commander himself who approached me and invited me to join the unit. Now, as for whether I felt the way you say I did, well, perhaps you're right. Yes. It was a different level of discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And that was the reputation of the Skorpions when you joined?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. They were held in high repute in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: For what reason?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, Western Srem, because that's where they were, in the area of Western Srem, Djeletovci. It's a small community. Everybody knows one another. There were some select men from the area and from Serbia who probably had been engaged in some actions before my arrival there and made themselves a name through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I have on the screen, please, D00205. And not to be shown to the public, please. In fact, perhaps we could go into private session for this, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. You may answer the question whether, to you knowledge, there was anyone else than Boca behind the unit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who was behind Boca? I think that was the question. Who stood behind Boca, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The question was -- well, I hope the question was: When you joined the Skorpions -- let me break it down a bit. Boca comes to you, and he asks you to join the Skorpions; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And at that point when he requests that you join, did you know anything about the Skorpions other than they guarded the oil wells?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the moment when I joined, I knew that they were a special unit, and that amongst other tasks, it was also tasked with guarding the oil wells.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And the special unit, what did you know about its creation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did I know then, or what I learnt subsequently? When I first joined, I didn't know much.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What did you know -- I know it may be tricky to put yourself back into that position, but what did you know then when Boca asked you to join?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Honestly, I knew that they were well equipped, that they were well paid, that they were a special unit not far from my home. That's all I pretty much knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when he asked you to join, did you answer right away, or did you take some time to think about it? How did it happen that you agreed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he took me to Djeletovci in a jeep. He wanted to show me the terminal and everything else. We spent three hours together inspecting the area, and then I told him that I agreed. Obviously, we discussed the matter of my salary, and three days later I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did you come by any information thereafter concerning who Boca reported to or who the special unit belonged to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I could understand at that moment. However, things were -- I'm absolutely certain that he reported to Milan Milanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And did you learn at that time who had created the unit and for what purposes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I learned from other senior Skorpion members who were also war commanders and who were privy to such details. The way I understood it was there had been a meeting in Novi Sad. Zivko Sokolovacki, Mrgud and I knew some other names at the time, and that Zivko Sokolovacki seems to have been the director of the Serbian oil industry. I don't know. In any case, that's where the agreement was reached for the oil wells to be reactivated and for a unit to be set up in order to secure the fields, and Mrgud personally put forth Medic as the organiser and commander of that future unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And Sokolovacki was the chairman of the Main Board of the oil company of Serbia, NIS; is that correct? NIS.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. Not in Nis, in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently you're using an acronym for the oil company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whereas the witness understands your reference to Nis as a reference to a location. The oil company, was it called NIS? And was Mr. Sokolovacki as I read it, but that's not what I heard, I think, was he the chairman of the Main Board of this oil company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the oil company is indeed NIS, the oil industry of Serbia, and Mr. Sokolovacki, whom I don't know was, as far as I know, supposed to be the CEO or the director of the general board of that company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It seems that the question has been answered. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it's time for a break within the next couple of minutes. Keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be a good moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This would be a good moment for a break, then we will have a break and we will resume at quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have on the screen, please, P1708.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, you'll recall this from yesterday, and to paraphrase, you said, Well, I don't think June is correct, because I was a member -- or I was engaged by the MUP of Serbia from August 1995 until December 1995. Do I summarise correctly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Had you seen this document before yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when did you see it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what did you tell the Prosecutor when you saw it in the office?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as I'm telling you, that I -- I believe that it was between the 11th of August and 22nd of November -- or December, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So when you were first shown this document, you told the Prosecution that their understanding of this document wasn't correct; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a woman, a lady Prosecutor, and that's what I told her.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When was that? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, during proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: When, roughly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of hours before I entered the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Before you entered the courtroom yesterday. Right. And was that lady writing notes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, you must know whether she had a piece of paper or a laptop in front of her and was either writing or tapping away on the keyboard while you were talking.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sitting a bit further away from her. She was sitting at her desk, and I was sitting a bit further away from her, and an interpreter was next to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What, did she have a pen in her hand?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, let's get to the core of what you want to establish. That's clear to all of us now, so let's get direct to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So that's one correction you gave to the Prosecution. Let's have a look if there's anything else. How long did the proofing sessions last before you came into court yesterday? I'm specifically talking about your proofing sessions in relation to your evidence yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very brief yesterday. I spent more time waiting for the proofing session to start. And the proofing session itself, I suppose it lasted for an hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And there was a proofing session the day before; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How long did that one last?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And were you taken through your 2003 statement?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We went through a couple of statements and some lists.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Paragraph by paragraph?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And this -- the lists were payment lists; is that correct? Lists indicating payments.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, payrolls.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you make various corrections to your statement during that proofing session or during both proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, there were corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: All right. Can we -- can we have on the screen, please, 65 ter 1D1733.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, what's going to come up, I hope, is the transcript of your testimony in the Belgrade court on the 12th of April, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I want, please, page 30 of the English and page 21 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now you recall this testimony, Mr. Witness? That was a question. Perhaps it didn't sound like one. Do you recall this testimony?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now if we look at page --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Actually, can we go back one page to -- no. Let's stay with that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, if we look towards the bottom of the page in English, at least, there's a discussion which you can read concerning supplies to the Skorpions, and you are asked at the bottom of the page -- or you make the comment -- sorry, the Presiding Judge asks you: "Tell me, did you have there some kind of magazine, there in that part where you were in Djeletovci? Was there some kind of magazine?" And then you talk about constructing a few houses, and one of those houses was used as a magazine: "Presiding Judge: Well, what was in the magazine? "Witness A. Well, weaponry, equipment, fuel. "Presiding Judge: Do you know?" Going over the page. "Witness A: Ammunition. "Presiding Judge: Do you know where those weapons came from? "Witness A: I was not a warehouseman. "Presiding Judge: Do you have any information about that? "Witness A: I can only guess, and I must not do that. "Presiding Judge: I'm asking if you have information. I know that you were not a warehouseman. And a couple of lines down: "Presiding Judge: From Yugoslavia but where from Yugoslavia? I mean who would give that to you? Who -- what would that be called? "Witness A: Well, probably both military and police." Am I correct that you were saying there, I actually don't know who supplied these -- this equipment which was stored in the magazine. Probably the police and the military. Is that a fair reading of what was happening during this testimony?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You saw that I answered the Judge that I didn't know. However, she insisted, and then I answered both the military and the police provided supplies, and I still believe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm not criticising you, but your position was you didn't know, and then the Judge put pressure on you and you expressed your belief; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And is it now, without pressure, your position that you just do not know who supplies the weaponry and other equipment to the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the answer will be the same. I don't know for sure. I can only assume, and I do assume that the supplies came both from the army and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me ask you then about your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, if the witness makes an assumption, I'd like to know on the basis of what he makes that assumption. If you're going to touch upon that matter, fine, if not --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'm a bit hesitant, not having been present and just on the basis of the reading, to -- to accept that pressure was put on the witness. Certainly the question was not put once to him. If you call that pressure, it could suggest that it is -- I would say a kind of pressure which should not have been put on a witness, and I would avoid such a judgement already at this moment without having looked at all of it. If you have good reasons for it, then we'd like to hear more about it, or perhaps after we've read all of it, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I was asking the witness if that was the case, and the witness said yes. I mean, we didn't -- I didn't have a position. I was trying to clarify what it was that made the witness turn from not knowing to expressing something more certain, and I asked him if there was pressure and he said yes, and that's as it is, according to the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let me have a closer look at it, but meanwhile, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could you, Mr. Witness, please, tell us what you base your assumption on that it was the military and the police who provided the weaponry and other equipment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is, I can tell you now, Mr. Jordash, what triggered my observation. Your question was: "And then the Judge put pressure on you, and you expressed your belief; correct?" The answer was: "Yes." That is two questions in one. He certainly expressed his belief, as you says, which is still his belief at this moment when he's not under pressure, which raises serious questions as to whether the witness felt that pressure was put upon him where he says, "I still believe that today." I hope that you are aware that you did ask two questions in one, and this is certainly not the best way of getting an answer. I don't think we have to explore the matter any further, but I thought it was on a rather light basis that you accepted this answer as an admission that pressure was put upon him. He certainly has expressed his belief where he said did he not have accurate knowledge. That seems to be clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you feel pressure, Mr. Witness, during that trial, in relation to this particular issue?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything is clear, because I can read my own language. The Judge asked me whether I know who had armed the unit. I said that I didn't know precisely, and then the Judge said, "Of course. You didn't work in a depot. You're not in a position to know." And then I said, "I can only assume." And then either he or she, I don't know who the Judge was, asked me to share that assumption with the Bench, and then I said that I assumed that both the military and the police had supplied us with -- with weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what was that assumption based on?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, we had members of the Krajina Army and the Yugoslav Army coming to the base as -- as well as members of the MUP. On one occasion we received a certain amount of pistols and were told that we received them from the MUP. On another occasion we received binoculars, and we were told again that they came from the MUP. We received lorries from the army though. It was based on this information that I concluded that both parties provided us supplies, but I didn't work in the warehouse to be sure of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how did you know they were from the MUP? Did they come in uniform?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see anyone bring these supplies, but when pistols were being distributed, we were told that it was a gift from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And which MUP?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody was explicit enough. Which other MUP was there save for the Yugoslav or the Serbian MUP? Well, yes, of course, we had the MUP in the Krajina, but where would they have come up with pistols from, and new ones at that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where did the MUP in Krajina get its weapons from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how the MUP of Krajina got hold of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did Mrgud obtain weapons from a factory in Serbia, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, you were told that weapons -- let's leave the military out of it for a moment. You were told that weapons were coming from a MUP, and from that you concluded that the police were providing some equipment. You -- am I understanding you correctly?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You were never told anything about the DB, whether the MUP referred to the DB or referred to the public security side of the MUP, whichever MUP was involved?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know that at the time the Ministry of the Interior and the ministry -- and the minister had a public and state security sector. Now, the MUP can mean either. Of course, there were the well-known stories surrounding the DB. In my mind, I cannot use a more proper term than that of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "In my mind, I cannot use a more proper term than that of the MUP," meaning exactly what? I'm not trying to catch you out. I'm just trying to clarify what you mean by --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get through this. Did I understand you well in your last answer that you wanted to say that when these weapons were distributed that when it was told that they came from the MUP that there were no further details, neither what MUP nor what part of the MUP or what section of the MUP? Is that correctly understood, that such details were not provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they weren't to me, and if they were, then I forgot them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And when you went through your statement with the Prosecution during proofing, did you talk about this subject?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About this trial in Belgrade, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Here. Did you tell the Prosecution here in the last few days of your two days of proofing that you didn't know one way or another which MUP was involved and whether, if it was the MUP, it was the state security or the public security? Did you tell the Prosecution that during the proofing sessions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall any such conversation, but we did discuss the DB and the MUP. I don't think we discussed the MUP of Krajina at all. I'm not sure. Or if we did, only slightly, but we did talk about the Serbian MUP and the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecution that the equipment you assumed had been provided by the MUP and the military, but you were not able to define who except in that general way?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do think I said that. That's to say that we received supplies from both the army and the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, but did you also say that you couldn't define it any further? Did you tell the Prosecution that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember. I can't remember if the Prosecutor went into such detail. What happened yesterday and the day before, well, it had to do with the MUP and the army. I don't remember the bit you're insisting on. Perhaps I was explaining it and can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, it's clear to me what your link is to the Belgrade document. Now, as far as I understand, that was apparently not discussed, because the Prosecutor informed us that he wasn't even aware that it was in their possession. Where exactly are we referring to, as far as the statements are concerned? I mean, that would be logical that -- to find a link anywhere in the statement where this specific issue would have come up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: The Belgrade document is in the possession of the Prosecution, because I've got the document here. This is on a different occasion when the witness testified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, this is a different --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Then I was confused by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, would Your Honour mind if I refer you to -- well, I can refer you to -- to the paragraph 73 of D1702, and if Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Let me just have a look. And I was exactly asking where.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That may also make it possible to be more focused in your questions. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I was hoping to put various things from the statement directly to the witness but not at this stage. I just want to go through a few other matters if I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you're mainly referring to the first two lines then.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's perfectly clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Am I correct that you were also visited by men from Sid and told that they were members of the MUP from Sid?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know every single member of the MUP of Sid. I didn't understand your question. Some people from Sid who were members of the MUP of Sid whom I didn't know, well, the town has 16.000 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Were you visited by anyone from Sid in an official capacity? When I say "you," I mean the Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were policemen arriving from Sid, and every morning, Commander Medic would go to Sid himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And do you know why they were attending, these policemen from Sid?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You were not visited by anyone from the DB, as far as you're aware, were you, from Sid?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- there were individuals from the DB there. They were present also at the time when we had to cross the bridge at Raca.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's leave the crossing at Raca out of it for the moment. There are individuals from the DB there. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it means. They would come.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: For what?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. They didn't meet up with me. I was just a platoon commander. They would go to the commander's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And how many would come and how often?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had certain tasks in Djeletovci. I didn't have a sentry post or stand guard in front of the commander's office. I can't tell you how often they would come, but they would come, various people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How did you know they were DB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because soldiers who were there would say that there were DB people. I saw cars which I assumed were from the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you ever see an identification saying that they were from the DB, the DB card?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the base, but I saw that card of an official of the DB.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what did it say on it to indicate that it was a card of the DB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a small booklet which said "DB." I didn't flip through it, but an official showed me that card when he was talking to me, and I can explain it to you how this came about. An operative of state security from Sremska Mitrovica spoke to me in Sid when a murder was committed in Kukujevci. Oskumic family was killed in Kukujevci. This individual knew that I was at the front line and knew some individuals who were at the front line, asked me if I had any information about the murder. Ultimately, the murder case was solved and a trial followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, do you speak any English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not so well, but not that bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, good enough, apparently. Well, I don't think there's any major problem in -- nevertheless, I would invite you to take your earphones off for a second. Mr. Jordash, what happens is the following: You ask, "How did you know that people coming were DB?" And the witness said, "Well, I was told they were DB," which is a clear indication that they did not identify them with the ID cards, because otherwise he would say, Well, they identified themselves by their ID. Then we move on with the IDs, and then, Have you ever seen such an ID, and the witness starts talking about an ID I have seen somewhere ever at another place, at another time, in another context. If we move on, we'll end up somewhere in Texas, policemen showing their identity stars. From that first answer, I don't know how you think our mind is working. If the witness says, We were told these were DB men, then unless some compelling evidence comes up, it is clear that no IDs were shown at the time. IDs were not the basis of the assumption or knowledge, call it whatever you want to call it, of the witness that this was delivered by the DB people. And this is not for the first time that this happens, and I want you to know that we are carefully listening and that we are not a jury, who, without having been explained, that this answer is most likely implying that no identity cards were shown at that time. We would not assume that unless there is any compelling evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, according -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's -- and now we are in a totally different place, totally different context. We are talking about whether he ever saw an ID. If you want to know whether he ever saw ID, but then unrelated, if you want, are you interested in knowledge of this witness on what is written on an ID, then ask him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I'm interested in paragraph 73, which has been admitted as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the witness has said, "The only thing I know is that I was told that they were DB," which for me, but I'm looking at my colleagues, whether they would do the same, means that there was no identification. It's just hearsay. Others said, "These are DB people." Then you can explore why these others would have said this if the witness knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: But I'm seeking to impeach the witness. In the evidence he's just given, no IDs; in his statement, IDs. And if -- if I leave it with the witness saying only that he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Jordash, that I had not carefully -- I focused so much on the first two lines of 73 that I wrongly stopped you here, and I apologise for that, and you're invited to continue. It is due to my colleagues, but your words should have been enough. I would not have needed my colleagues to come to your assistance. I should have listened to you more clarify, and I should have read more carefully. My apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness -- could you put up your earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's try to shortcut things. I'm not interested, Mr. Witness, in members of the DB coming to investigate a particular crime. I'm not interested at this point in time, at least. What I'm interested in is whether you ever saw a DB identification card in the possession of somebody coming to visit the Skorpions, whether Boca or Mrgud or someone connected in that way.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise for the fact that I wanted to give you an illustration when I told you of that instance when a DB representative showed his ID card to me. So I did see the card, but back at the Skorpions' base, nobody identified themselves to me. I suppose that they -- their arrival would normally be announced. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to give a more detailed description of what the card looked like, the ones that you did see, the Serbian DB cards? Besides the words "DB" written on them, was there everything else?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. It was like a booklet. You would open it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Anything else indicating it belonged to the DB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the ID card in my hands. The individual flapped it open in front of me, said that he was a DB official and asked that we have a word. The booklet did appear to me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat what he just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your answer. The interpreters did not catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have the DB official's ID card in my hands. The operative or representative of the DB took out his card, introduced himself, and asked me to talk to him. And that was it. That's how I saw what the card looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What colour was the card, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was red.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. But basically a once-only affair. You caught a glimpse, and you're unable to say much else.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we go, please, to P1702. Actually, that's where we are. Could we go to the next page, please. Now, I want you to focus on paragraph 78, and then I'm going to read it: "We built a whole headquarters complex at Djeletovci, including accommodation, gyms, et cetera. Our expenses were paid by the DB and by the Krajina Oil Company which provided most of our funds. I was issued an identification booklet by the Skorpions with my photo and rank. It indicated that I was a member of MUP Serbian state security. My identification booklet did not say SRK, it said Republic of Serbia. It also authorised me to requisition vehicles and communication equipment as needed. This was the same authorisation that members of the DB had."

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I begin to answer without the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, the question is obvious, isn't it? Why does your statement say this concerning your possession of a Serbian state security card? That's the first question.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This particular booklet was read, and it said the Skorpions. There was a photo and rank. We had the right to use communication means and vehicles of others. It said the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, but it said the MUP. Your statement says the DB. That's the issue I would like you, if you would, to address.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't read in great detail what the actual real DB card said. I suppose that there you could also read the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: "I couldn't read in great detail what the actual real DB said. I suppose that there you could also read the MUP." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because the DB is part of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday, when dealing with IDs, you said the booklet, and I'm looking at page 22 of the draft transcript: "All our officers and non-commissioned officers were issued IDs, red booklets with the inscription 'The Skorpion unit.' The booklet depicted the person's name and the rank. And then on the last page of the booklet it said that the owner of the ID could use anybody's communication means or anybody's vehicle." So yesterday you moved away from the suggestion that the DB -- that your card recorded the DB. Do you now say, My card - I want to be clear about this -- I did not have a card with 'DB' written on it. Do you say that now?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am absolutely sure that the booklet contained stamps, that it wrote "Certified by MUP," followed by certain numbers, and I couldn't give you any more details what with the lapse of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to belabour the point and I'm going to move on, but did you ever tell the Prosecution that this part of your statement was in error? Did you ever say it's not correct during the proofing over the last two days?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if the paragraph was in the proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. If you can't or won't remember, then let's move back to paragraph 73 of this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to get matters as clear as we can. In this statement, you say that your booklet indicated that you were a member of the MUP Serbia State Security DB. Is it that you say now that you're certain that it indicated whether through stamps or another way that the booklet was issued under the authority of the MUP, but that you're not sure any more whether it indicated that you were -- that it was the DB of the MUP which certified it or that you were a member of ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Let me explain. I gave this statement seven years ago about an event that happened 11 years ago. In hindsight, well, this was already, you know, seven years ago, and it's been 18 years since the event, and, in the meantime, perhaps I saw a document that refreshed my memory. What I can remember at this stage is a stamp issued by the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Without reference to the DB.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my view, but I'm again not absolutely sure. Even if it is the DB, it says the MUP, the security services sector. In other words, the first thing you see is the "MUP."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I suggest, sir, that you understand the picture, Mr. Witness, that you couldn't have had a Serbian DB card, because Serbian DB cards did not exist? If they had, the Prosecution, after 15 years of investigation, would have them.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a bit after provocation, I would say. Well, in that case, it turns out that our commander did it all himself. He designed the booklets. He had them printed. He distributed them of its own will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're speculating on the basis of what you just heard, isn't it, whether the commander did it himself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not me, Your Honour. I did have a booklet. I returned the booklet. And not just me. All the officers, even all the drivers, had the booklets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You do not accept that they did not exist or at least that IDs with such stamps in it did not exist, because you say, I had one. All of the officers had one, and even the drivers had one. The matter is clear, at least, that there is a disagreement on this, a matter between the Prosecution and the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. May we go, please, to 1D1733.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We're going back to the transcript of your testimony in the Belgrade court on the 12th of April, 2006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, could you help me. The pressure page, I couldn't find it anymore, which one it was, in e-court. The earlier one, you remember, that -- where I was a bit hesitant to talk about pressure. What page was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: -- page 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 31. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't know if that's the e-court number but it's the page of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'll find it. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to page 93 of the English and 61 of the B/C/S. Page 61 of the B/C/S and page 93 of the English. And I want to -- 93 of the English. 93. Sorry, 93 of the English. Ah, that's it. Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me take you to the -- a third of the way down the -- the page. A member of the Trial Chamber asked you: "You said officially we were officially with the Loncar corps, the Loncar corps. "Witness A: Well it cannot be. I beg your pardon. "Yes, yes," says the member of the Trial Chamber. "Witness A: Corps is one huge formation and it has its commander. No one can be in the corps area of responsibility without being subordinated to this particular corps and to this particular commander, in my opinion. Say if we were stationed in Djeletovci, in Djeletovci, regardless of the financing, partly we had to report to that particular corps. Then again, we would receive a part of our orders from this particular corps, not myself personally, but my commander who would then transfer these orders upon us. After all, we hold a large portion of the border, and the corps were supposed to know about that." Do you stand by that answer? Is that a yes or -- do you stand by that answer?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you that we had other tasks besides guarding the oil fields, and that was also guarding the border, which was all within the purview of the corps, and in that sense it was the corps that gave us the relevant orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did orders come from the Main Staff in relation to the guarding of the border? The Main Staff of --

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From General --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could the witness please repeat the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Repeat the name, please.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From General Loncar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Not from Celeketic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a man who went by that name also, but I believe that Celeketic was inferior to General Loncar, but I'm not sure. In any case, the name does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's deal with the point that I'm really interested in which is underneath that paragraph. When you were asked by the same member of the Trial Chamber: "Yes, did you personally have any identification card confirming that you were actually a member of this unit or anything?" Your answer: "Yes, they -- they did have them. Many a Skorpion showed me their ID cards, but at the time I had been with them, these cards had not been issued yet. I never had one. Member of the Trial Chamber: "So you have in the been in possession of any ID card, is that so? "A. You see, I left the Skorpioni but I still frequented the areas where they were deployed."

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so. I did not have an ID or a document from day one. I suppose this refers to a certain period and whether at that moment I had it or not. I received documents towards the very end.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, you didn't tell the Belgrade court that, did you? You left the distinct impression you never had one. "I never had one." It's not an impression, it's what you said.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't see -- I'm absolutely convinced that I answered questions about a certain period and whether during that certain period I had a document or not. This is what my answers to the Judge were about.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Where is the ID card you say you had? Where is it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There came a time when Srdjan Manojlovic took all the documents and some equipment from all unit members. As far as I know, one or two acquaintances of mine did not return their IDs. To this very day they haven't returned them, whereas the rest of us, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So you did give the Prosecution your booklet relating to your time with the JNA but were not able to give your ID card for the Skorpions. Were you ever actually a member of the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was. I was a member of the Skorpions. My military booklet was in my possession, so I handed it over, whereas the other thing was no longer in my possession, hence I couldn't hand it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you inform the Prosecution that you knew ex-Skorpions who had identification cards still in their possession?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the investigators -- not the prosecutors, but the investigators did make inquiries, and when they did, I told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You told them where to find them, did you? Who had them? Where they might be located?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat, if the investigator asked me that, I'm sure that I told him that I knew who was still in the possession of the cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we have on the screen, please, 1D1728.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's your testimony in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't think there's a problem with me announcing any testimony in public, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I don't believe the witness has ever had protective measures. I can't speak whether the particular portion that you're referring to is in closed session or not, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you. You're right. It was in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's the Milutinovic trial, Mr. Witness, where you testified for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And could we go to page 693. And it's page 12 -- 11 of e-court, I hope. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now, we're moving back to the issue of subordination and other issues, and you can see you're asked the question at line 2: "Now, what kind of organisation or group was the Skorpions? Was it a military unit, a social unit, an army unit, if you know?" You answer there and give some details about its structure, and then at line 9 you're asked the question: "Well, that's my question. You mentioned uniforms. What kind of uniforms did the Skorpions have? "A. They weren't always the same. As far as I know, they always had better uniforms than the Serb army. It was more up to date, more modern. "Q. Were the Skorpions a part of the JNA? "A. No. "Q. Who did they belong to, if anyone? "A. From what I know, officially they were supposed to be part of the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. I also know that a lot of influence over this unit was wielded from the MUP of Serbia, although I don't know how this came about or how it was materialised." Do you stand by that, that you don't know how the influence of the MUP of Serbia came about or how it was materialised?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've been talking about this the whole morning. I know that there were contacts with the MUP, but I can't say whether they sent us orders or not. I received my orders from my commander, and I executed them, but as to what you have just now read, what I had previously stated, I adhere by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Right. You don't know if anyone from the MUP of Serbia had any commanding role over the Skorpions, do you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mrgud or Milan Milanovic gave us orders. Sometimes General Loncar did as well. And Mrgud is the one who travelled to Belgrade, at least that's what I heard. He travelled to Belgrade to receive his instructions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You don't know who he met there, do you? You don't know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Only once I heard from him that he had met with a high-ranking officer known as Badza.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Apart from him, you don't know if he met anyone else at all, other than this one occasion when he met Badza?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that because he said that once in the office, that he had met with Badza. But I believe that when he went to Belgrade, he met with everybody from the MUP. At the end of the day, that's what he told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I suggest that Mrgud never told you that he met with Stanisic. Could that be right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to me. He never said any such thing to me. He may have said it to Medic, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, let's not deal with what you don't know. If he never said it to you, then we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let's go to page 696 of this transcript, and page 14 of e-court. Actually, let's not. Let's leave that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I just briefly take instructions, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Let me ask you briefly about registration plates. Am I correct that at the time you were in the Skorpions, M601 was a registration plate which indicated nothing more than the vehicle was registered in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what that meant, but I don't think it was 601. It was either 602 or 606, but that was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. So your understanding, then, is that 602 or 606 indicated nothing more than the vehicle came from Serbia; correct? Let me break that down for you. 602, I suggest, indicated that the vehicle came from Croatia. Could that be right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.
