utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: 606, what did that indicate to you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All police registration plates seemed identical to me, but rumours had it that those numbers were reserved for the DB vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Witness, you travelled into Serbia on many occasions, didn't you, during these years? You must have known, I suggest, that M601 indicated not that the vehicle belonged to the police, but that it just was a vehicle registered in Serbia; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I never studied the police vehicles' registration plates. And if DB officials were in the car, then they probably had civilian registration plates. I don't know. I'm just telling you what I heard in Krajina, what stories had at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to -- while we're on this transcript, let's go to page 111 of e-court and page 793 of the transcript itself. And we're going to return very briefly to the subject of ID cards, something you said here. I just want to ask you for some clarification on some

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we go down the page, please. Not that far. A bit further up. That's fine there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were asked the question: "Mr. Stoparic, are you aware of the fact, or do you know what kinds of military service booklets the other members of the Skorpions had and was it connected with the places from which they came? "A. I see that there is a misunderstanding here. I said simply if you were Serb from Serbia your address was there. I didn't say Serbian in the sense of Serbia proper. You had your address, and it was written whether it -- "Q. Who actually issued these booklets? "A. Manojlovic brought them. As far as I can remember, they had been made in Vukovar, and it had something to do with the Krajina." Could you explain that last answer, please: "As far as I remember, they had been made in Vukovar, and it had something to do with the Krajina"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's probably what I remembered at the time. I remember at the time that Manojlovic told us they were from Vukovar, and the connection with Krajina is the fact that Vukovar was the capital of Krajina. And as I sit here today, yes, I believe that he did bring them from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm having "Break" shouted out from behind me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's time we had a break. We will take a break and resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's now the second time that we return so late. I can assure the parties that at least this time we spent all of this time on this case. So if that would be of any consolation, may it be so. Mr. Jordash, are you ready to proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about special units of the VRS and the relationship between them and the DB of Serbia during the war, during the time you were in the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska or of the Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Army of Republika Srpska was much more serious than that of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina. They had many special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything about them and their relationship to the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I need to be prompted by a specific unit to remember anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't have any units in mind. I just want to know if you do, because you do make a connection with them in your statement, and I'm wondering if you actually have any knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do have some knowledge, though not direct one, that these units had some ties with the Red Berets or -- either because they were trained in their camps or by their instructors. I know that there were ties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So it's just the training, is it? Is that the ties you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm 100 per cent sure about training. Such a unit could only have provided the best possible training for anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which units do you have in mind of the Republika Srpska -- Army of Republika Srpska? Can you name them?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Pesa's unit underwent such training, as did some Drina Wolves. I can't remember at this time. There were several such units bearing such names.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have, please, page 55 of the transcript we have on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you about something else. And you're being asked here during this trial, just to remind you, this is the Milutinovic trial, and you're asked about the CSB Doboj, and you answer there at paragraph 16 -- or just have a look at the top page -- top of the page, sorry, just to get your bearings.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I have is in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course it is. Sorry. Let me read something to you then. You're asked the question: "Do you want to say that the CSB Doboj was a satellite auxiliary unit of, I think, the DB?" And you answer: "No, probably only their special platoon or special company. "Q. One part of the CSB, therefore? "A. Please, I apologise if I made a mistake somewhere in these acronyms. Whenever I heard over the communication lines 'CSB' or words to that effect, I thought that they referred to their specialists. I know that, generally speaking, in police terms the CSB is something larger." Do you remember that evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that your knowledge of the CSB Doboj is limited in the way suggested by this evidence?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I don't know much about them. I met them out in the field around Sarajevo, and that's how they referred to them, the CSB Doboj specialists under the command of an individual they referred as Zenga.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right. And apart from that, you don't know who they reported to; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably to the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's read on. You were asked a question about your statement, your statement of 2003, and it says this: "Paragraph 73 on page 19, that's page 14 in the English version. You state: 'The state security of the RSK did not exist. There was only the state security of Serbia?'" "You're speaking of the structure of the MUP in the Republic of the Serbian Krajina?" Going over the page. The question then is at line 1: "Paragraph 73 of your statement states there was no state security of the RSK." You answer: "Yes. That's as far as I know. "Q. Do you know that for a fact or as a rumour? "A. I wasn't a responsible duty holder there. You could say that I heard that." Now, were you effectively saying that you didn't know one way or another, you heard there was no state security of the RSK, but you didn't know?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that's how I answered the question, i.e., that I truly didn't know. I said what I knew. I didn't think that there existed a structure called the state security of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina or Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, further down the page you -- I'm not taking issue with this at all, I'm just trying to understand your evidence. At line 21, you say in relation to this issue: "You see, sir, if something is said 100 times, even if it is an untruth, it will being the truth. To me, as an ordinary person, a soldier, I simply had to grasp pieces of information and make conclusions on the basis of that." And do you stand by that? There's lots of information you heard effectively as rumours, repeated rumours. This is in large part, when you speak about the state security of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina, that's what you base it on.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. There was a lot of confusion and rumours around, and I can claim what I said then even today. If something is -- that is a lie is stated for a hundred times, it will become the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. And it was -- there was lots of rumours about the state security of Serbia at that time; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that you heard rumours that the CSB of Doboj was connected to the DB? That was rumours.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I heard something of the sort in company over a cup of coffee, then I would call it a rumour. It's not an official information, a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you hear of a connection over a cup of coffee between the CSB of Doboj and the state security of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, over a cup of coffee or without it, well, I had this knowledge about the connection existing, and to tell you the truth, I don't see anything strange in that. After all, we are a one people.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let's just leave out of it for the moment whether it's strange, but you didn't know who the CSB reported to, did you, as you've indicated two or three minutes ago? You assumed the MUP of Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would that be the case also in relation to, let's say, the Wolves from Vucak? Who did they report to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about -- do you know a group called the Gumars -- sorry, the Vipers commanded by Gumar? Do you know of them? Do you know if this group existed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the name Gumar, I did hear of it, and I heard of a group called Horned Vipers, if that's got to do with this. Poskoci. I suppose that he did have something to do with the state security of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, what do you suppose? What did they have to do with the state security of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. They were organised, trained, equipped, along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By who in the state security of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how they were organised. The story was that Simatovic was the boss for these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You never saw anything to indicate that you heard rumours; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Simatovic after all these events, on television. We knew his nickname. There's nothing that would enable me to state that with a hundred per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, you've watched the Kula video, haven't you? The video with Mr. Simatovic giving a speech; correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Once, a long time ago, investigators showed me the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When were you shown that video? Can you remember? You'd seen it, hadn't you, before the 2003 statement, your first statement on the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be precise, but it was a long time ago that I saw the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, could I ask you, could we ask one additional question. You said, "Once, a long time ago, investigators showed me the video." Now, which investigators? Were these ICTY investigators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I remember the names of the investigators. The investigators of the ICTY, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they show it to you before they interviewed you, during the interview, after the interview? Do you remember? Or in the course of the interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it was during an interview. I am sure that I saw the video-clip in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I refer Your Honour to paragraph 70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen P1702, which I think might cast some light on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is your statement of 2003. And I don't think we're in dispute here at all, Mr. Witness. I just want you to see something specific in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Paragraph 70, 14 of e-court, please. Fourteen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue may be that it's a bit unclear about the course of the interviews during these days. One thing is for sure, that it was signed on the 24th, I think, but two -- quite a couple of days. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 70. You invent a theory that: "The Red Berets were the base, the skeleton of all the DB special units. The other units such as the Skorpions were satellites. The other satellite units I know of were the Grey Wolves from the Zvornik, CSB from Doboj, Arkan's Tigers, the Wolves from Vucak and the Vipers commanded by Gumar." Can I try to shorten things. Given your answers concerning such groups as the CSB and the Vipers and your lack of knowledge about them, that this statement is based on nothing more than rumours, people talking, whether at the time or since then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I always drew a distinction between what I knew first-hand and hearsay or my opinions. So that's how I formulated my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, this paragraph doesn't read like that. It doesn't indicate that you knew this from what you were told, what you picked up from rumours. It indicates something a bit more certain than that. Did you tell the Prosecution you had gathered this information from rumours, from what people told you rather than something more concrete?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the investigators would always put questions to me: How did this work? Where did you hear of it? And I would give my answers accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let's just read on in the paragraph to the section which says: "Apart from the special MUP units, there were also special units of the VRS that were supplied by the DB." We dealt with that a moment ago: "Whenever special units in Bosnia were formed there was at least one guy from the Red Berets and he would give them equipment from the DB as a 'gift.' Frenki basically says as much on the Kula ceremony video." So am I correct that you saw that video prior to giving the substance of this paragraph to the Prosecution investigators?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this unambiguously shows that I had seen the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did you -- did you express any doubt to the investigators when telling them about this theory concerning the Red Berets and the satellites? Did you say where that information had come from?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would ask that as a rule, because they wanted to satisfy themselves of it, and I would answer depending on the question where I heard it, where I saw it, or whether it was an inference I made based on a number of pieces of information I had, and that was how I answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that this paragraph is a combination of rumours and what you saw on the Kula video, or do you have more direct evidence than that?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what to tell you. It contains what I, at that point, thought of the subject involved. It contains what I knew, and it may include rumours. In fact, stories that I heard, and you call them rumours. I don't know what to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- just before we leave this subject, let me go back to 65 ter 1D1728.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I notice at this moment that apparently the definition of what a rumour is, where the witness earlier said that if it was not official information but matters he heard, that is hearsay information, that he called all of that rumours. Now, at the same time, in his last answers where you, I don't know whether you intended to adopt his definition of "rumours," but if you did so, then the witness now in his answer is a bit more limited in what he calls rumours. It's what he heard that includes all, I would say, informal hearsay evidence. He would not necessarily and automatically accept that as being rumours. There is a bit of a conceptual distinction. I'm not seeking at this moment to further clarify that, but I just noticed it, and thought it appropriate to put it on the record. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me just try to wrap up this subject, Mr. Witness. Did you ever see anything to indicate a relationship from the Grey Wolves from near Zvornik and the DB of Serbia? Did you see anything?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must tell you that I had never been involved in any operations with the Grey Wolves, or if I had, then I was unaware of it. In respect of the Grey Wolves, the only information I could provide you is, as His Honour the Judge said, rumours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And does that also apply to Arkan's Tigers?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, the Arkan's Tigers were the most serious paramilitary unit and had most certainly enjoyed some sort of state sponsorship.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, had most certainly enjoyed some sort of state sponsorship. Is this what you were told at the time, and, if so, by whom?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a moment ago you showed us a document which need not be shown to the public. Am I allowed to talk about it now then?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Certainly, but perhaps we should go into private session if it is something we already dealt with in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move into private session out of an abundance of caution.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have, please, 1D1728, please. I think that might be what we're looking at. And could we have page 12 of e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I want to just give you -- or just seek some clarification. Now, you're speaking here about -- well, let's go back one page so that we get the context. And what -- if we go to line 16, and I'll remind you we've gone through this already, but just so there's context. You say: "From what I know, officially," this is the Skorpions, "they were supposed to be part of the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. I also know that a lot of influence over the unit was wielded from the MUP, although I don't know how this came about or how it was materialised." And then over the page, line 11, you say: "Some other group. To my knowledge when we had meetings with the commander and he gave us assignments and from conversations with other members of the unit, they always said it was the ... state security that was behind that unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I believe you missed a word, "Serb state security."

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. That really was unintentional.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's not speculate about whether it was Freudian or not, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "... they always said it was the ... state security that was behind that unit? "Q. And there's an abbreviation for the Serb state security that you use in your statement? "A. It wasn't used by me, it was used by everyone, and it was the DB." Now, are you suggesting that in this testimony that every time you were given an order, you were told it was directly from the state security of Serbia? Is that really what you're suggesting there?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were you saying then or trying to convey?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, on one occasion Medic told me this: The border belongs to the military and the oil wells to the state security, because the latter facility was of a strategic importance. That's what he meant when he said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Just reading further down, and the question is then asked: "In your statement in paragraph 10, you mention the Red Berets as being the skeleton of all DB ... units. You mention the Skorpions as being a satellite. Were you aware of other satellite units? "A. According to the stories at the time and based on what I know now, those were Arkan's Tigers, too, and there were some other units in the Republika Srpska, yes, in Bosnia." And my question is: What did you mean when you said "and based on what I know now"?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is no secret that trials had already started in Serbia. I took part in some of them. Judgements were passed, final judgements were passed, and I concluded based on that, that that was why Arkan's Tigers were the first, that there must have been a link there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the answer. Let's move now to Trnovo. Now, are you able to identify now for the Trial Chamber which men were responsible for shooting the prisoners? Can you just name them so that we're clear on who it was shot the unfortunate men?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, would you.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you going to show me a document, or do you want me to just give you the names off the top of my head?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please excuse me if I ask you to do it off the top of your head because I'm not quite clear myself yet and I want to be clear before I start. I'm not trying to trick you, and I will almost certainly have no dispute with you on the issue.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan Medic had the command responsibility because he ordered the executions, and the executors were Pera Petrasevic, Medic -- actually, there were two names by the name of Medic. I may even confuse them now. Okay, let me take them in different order. Pera Petrasevic; Milorad or Miodrag Momic; Branislav Medic, also known as Zekan; and Aleksandar Medic; and that guy from Croatia, Bodo. What was his name? Sometimes I just seem to forget his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Miodrag or Milorad was Momic. There is a man who was convicted in Zagreb for the same crime, and we used to call him Bodo, and his name was -- it will come to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Microphone not activated] Six, I think you've named.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And may I, for Your Honours' information, just indicate at this stage that there's an agreement between the Prosecution and the Defence that the names of the Skorpion members identified and/or convicted as direct perpetrators of the killings of the six men at Trnovo in July 1995 are not on the state security payment records provided by the government of Serbia to date. And just to be complete with -- there's another agreement which is that the name of Goran Stoparic appears on the above -- appears on those payment records provided to date during the period starting on the 16th of August and ending on the 15th of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is agreed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that's on the record. I think I did understand you well that we are -- that you agreed what is found on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you about these men who were the perpetrators. Am I correct that only Pera Petrasevic was, in fact, a combatant in the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I did not understand your question. They were all Skorpion members. Pera Petrasevic, however, was the most willing in the group, in military terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, for example, what -- okay. Let's go through the names. What did Aleksandar Medic do in the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, you early used the word "combatant." It took me quite a while studying quite a lot of books to understand fully what a combatants is. Apart from newly-developed terminology, if you could keep it as factual as possible in this respect it would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me try to break this down. This group of men, were they acting at the time of the killings as security to the commander? Was that their principal function at the time of the killings?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, save for Branislav Medic who was a driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And so their job was not to attend the front line but to keep Medic secure as he moved around; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So to that extent, they were out of the ordinary chain of command when it came to defending the front line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No platoon commander or company commander could issue them any orders. Only the commander could do that. So they held a privileged position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And did they obtain their position as security because they had particularly good relationships with the commander?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Save for Pera Petrasevic, everybody else did. They were even godfather's to each other's children and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this was a group of men who were friends of old, before the Trnovo operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It applies to all of them but Petrasevic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And none of them received orders from anyone else other than Medic, is that correct, the commander?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is corrected, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And none of them gave orders to anyone else; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes they acted as internal control for the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right. So do you mean by that they acted as some form of military police at times, or do you mean something different?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes if there was an incident involving two soldiers, any kind of incident, then the commander would send them to investigate, and after that the soldiers sometimes were even punished.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that where the Commander Medic lived or where he was billeted was at least two kilometres from the enemy lines, from the front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While he resided in Krajina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, whilst at Trnovo. Where was Medic billeted in relation to the front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand. Two kilometres as the crow flies, but it was certainly even a bit further away from the front line if you travelled by road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when this killing event occurred, were the majority of the Skorpions at the front line? What was the situation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half, plus the Reconnaissance Platoon. Half of the company was on the front line. The other half was in the makeshift base. And that was done on purpose, so we could take shift without waiting for anybody else to replace us on the front line. And for us Reconnaissance Platoon members, we were on the front line all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where was the makeshift base, then, in relation to the front line?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to Trnovo, it was a kilometre, 2 kilometres away from town. Before the war, it was a settlement of weekend cottages. Those were actually weekend cottages. We were billeted there, and those weekend cottages served as our base.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So half of the Skorpions were at the front line at the time of this killing. And am I understanding you correctly: The other half were at the makeshift base? And sorry if I'm being slow, but how far was the makeshift base from where the killings took place?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely, but I did inspect the area on foot several times, and in my view the execution place was not more than 4 to 5 kilometres away from Medic's base, and you had to travel uphill partly by lorry and partly by foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. So just to understand this correctly, the Skorpion group, aside from the security, were not at the killing site; am I correct? They were at the front line or the makeshift base, both of which were several kilometres away, or at least 2 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Save for the perpetrators, there were some other Skorpion members who, before the execution actually took place, left the front line and then returned to the base, whereas one or two remained at the killing site and attended the act of execution. And let me explain. When we heard the sound of the lorry on the front line, and they brought the prisoners by lorry, then usually the first thing that came to mind was that you were being replaced or that the provisions had arrived, cigarettes or food or something like that. Then the commander would normally send one or two of us to go to the lorry and fetch all that. And if the equipment on the lorry was on a heavy side, then we would haul it by smaller vehicles or animals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So how many Skorpions would you estimate were around or in the immediate vicinity of the killing site other than the direct perpetrators and also you?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not so close to the killing site. Two or three men were in the immediate vicinity of the killing site, and they observed the entire thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And how many were, say, within your kind of distance, 200 -- 200 metres or so?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was another man together with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. So it's six perpetrators, two or three men in the immediate vicinity, you and another man 200 metres away, the remainder of the Skorpions at least 2 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the camera guy who was there as well. I forgot to mention him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. But apart from that, the remainder of the Skorpions 2 kilometres away, at least.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Skorpions who were on the front line were about 2 kilometres away, whereas the others who were on the base at the time, they were about 4 or 5 kilometres away from the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Now, I want to try to clear up something. Am I correct that when the prisoners were delivered to the -- where were they delivered to, please? The location in relation to the killing site.

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far -- now let me go back a bit. Am I correct that you actually didn't see the prisoners being delivered? You actually saw the vehicle which had transported them leaving; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, you're not right. The prisoners were brought to the improvised base a bit further away near Trnovo. I was there, and I saw the prisoners being delivered, and then they were loaded onto the truck, and I left. I left before them, because I knew that they would follow me. So when the truck pulled over, there were some 200 -- 2- to 300 metres away from me, and there was a distance in height. I was about 20 to 30 metres above them on the sloping ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to remind you of something you said in Belgrade, and I'm not trying to catch you out, because I acknowledge it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can we have on the screen 65 ter 1D1733, please. And could we go to page 49 of the transcript and page 34 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, I'll read from the Presiding Judge in the middle of the page says the following: "Presiding Judge: Let me just ask you: Were you there when they arrived on the spot beside the weekend cottage? "Witness A: Not exactly beside the weekend cottage. They already -- the people already got out, those six ones that we're talking about or seven. I do not know. They were already taken out. They were standing beside the weekend cottage, or they were, I don't know. They were supposed to be taken somewhere already or locked up at that moment. I was already nearby." And then if we go over the page to page 50, 34 of the B/C/S: "And then they continued further with the bus -- with bus, didn't they?" This is the Presiding Judge. "Witness A: Yes, they continued doing their job. "Presiding Judge: Did you see that bus at all? "Witness A: While it was departing. "Presiding Judge: While it was departing? "Witness A: Yes." Further down the page, Presiding Judge who has also taken your answer as the bus leaving says: "All right. You saw the bus that was leaving. Were there any other people in the bus? "Witness A: I gave a look. I assumed that that was it, that they were those prisoners, there were some other people, whether there were only those from the escort inside the bus or there were some other prisoners as well. I think that there were some more prisoners since they looked sort of shabby and miserable." So could it be that you've put together information and, in fact, the reality was that you saw the prisoners standing and the bus leaving rather than anything more in terms of the bus being there, the prisoners getting out, and so on? Could it be prisoners, bus departing?

utterances.speaker: GORAN STOPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I don't really understand you, or are you trying to confuse me on purpose? I saw the prisoners when they were brought and when the bus left, but I was leaving the base. I was leaving for the front line, and that was what my mind was preoccupied with, and then what I thought about the bus was that that bus was simply transporting people to different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I'm looking at the clock. I thought five minutes ago when you started introducing your next question that we would finish within time, but I have to interrupt here. We adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I indicate that I've got five minutes left and I've spoken to Mr. Bakrac and he's happy for me to take five minutes tomorrow, and then I've finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And will then Mr. Bakrac also finish tomorrow, because that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. My colleague has just saved me some time with asking some of the questions that he did, so I can be generous and give him the five minutes and still finish tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you also perhaps meet with Mr. Groome and see how much time would be left for him then, and then inform the Chamber so that we would know how much time we still have. Mr. Stoparic, I would like to instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony, that is, whether already given yesterday or today or whether still to be given tomorrow. So speak with no one, communicate with no one, and we would like to see you back tomorrow in the afternoon because we adjourn for today and we resume tomorrow, Thursday, the 16th of December, quarter past 2.00 in this came courtroom, II.
